items.title: Isomorphism classes of torsors under an abelian sheaf are classified by first cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement identifies two objects that are built by completely different means: isomorphism classes of H-torsors on a site and the first cohomology group H^1(C, H) of an abelian sheaf (statement lines 292-295). The proof has to construct both directions explicitly. The first construction is a pushout followed by a boundary operator: it forms the free abelian sheaf on the torsor, its augmentation sigma, the map a from Ker(sigma) to H determined by the torsor action through h.s' = s, pushes the sequence defining Z[F] out along a, and takes the image of 1 under the connecting homomorphism (proof lines 299-333). The second is a representability argument that needs an injective embedding, the vanishing of H^1 of an injective sheaf, and the identification of the preimage of a global section of Q = I/H as a torsor (proof lines 336-356). What the author does not do is verify that the two constructions are mutually inverse; that verification is declared omitted at proof lines 358-360 and is retained verbatim in the delivered item, so the bijection itself is asserted by the author and not carried out in the printed argument.
